questions.q: Where did the tailor sit while he sewed all day?
choices: In the window of his shop, cross-legged on a table
By the fire in his kitchen in College Court
On a bench outside the big Cathedral
In a chair beside his four-post bed
questions.evidence: He sat in the window of a little shop in Westgate Street, cross-legged on a table

questions.q: What was the tailor himself like?
choices: Rich and stout, with fine silk clothes and rings
Very poor, old, and in thread-bare clothes
Young and strong, with a loud voice
Cross and mean to everyone he met
questions.evidence: he himself was very, very poor

questions.q: Who was the tailor making a coat for?
choices: The Mayor of Gloucester
A rich London merchant
The King of England
Himself, for Christmas

questions.q: What one thing was missing before the coat could be finished?
choices: Yellow taffeta for the lining of the coat
A skein of cherry-coloured twisted silk
Twelve pieces of satin
A box of shiny gold buttons
questions.evidence: there was wanting just one single skein of cherry-coloured twisted silk

questions.q: What was the name of the tailor's cat?
choices: Tabitha
Simpkin
Ginger
Moppet
questions.evidence: He lived alone with his cat; it was called Simpkin.

questions.q: What was the last penny of the fourpence meant to buy?
choices: A penn'orth of sausages for supper
A penn'orth of milk for Simpkin
A penn'orth of cherry-coloured silk
A candle to light up the dark little shop
questions.evidence: buy me one penn'orth of cherry-coloured silk

questions.q: What did the tailor find under the upside-down tea-cups?
choices: Mice
Coins
Silk
Thread
questions.evidence: Out stepped a little live lady mouse

questions.q: Why was Simpkin so cross when he came home?
choices: He had lost the groat on his way to market
The mice he wanted for supper were gone
The tailor had eaten all the sausages
He had broken the china pipkin
questions.evidence: He wanted his supper of little fat mouse!

questions.q: Where did Simpkin hide the twist?
choices: Under the bed
In the tea-pot
In the coal-box
Behind the dresser
questions.evidence: Simpkin hid a little parcel privately in the tea-pot

questions.q: What happened to the tailor after Simpkin hid the twist?
choices: He went to the shop and worked all night
He became very ill with a fever
He went out to buy more silk himself
He chased the mice all over the town
questions.evidence: the poor old tailor was very ill with a fever

questions.q: The tailor says "Alack, I am undone!" What does he mean?
choices: I am finished with my work
I am in great trouble
I am going to bed now
I am very rich today

questions.q: In the old story, what can all the beasts do on Christmas Eve night?
choices: Fly
Talk
Swim
Grow
questions.evidence: all the beasts can talk, in the night between Christmas Eve and Christmas Day

questions.q: What did Simpkin see when he peeped into the tailor's shop that night?
choices: The shop was dark and empty
It was full of candles and mice sewing and singing
Cats dancing in the garret to the sound of a fiddle
The Mayor trying on his new coat

questions.q: Why could Simpkin not get into the shop?
choices: The mice were holding the door shut
The key was under the tailor's pillow
The snow had piled up against the door
The window was much too high to reach
questions.evidence: But the key was under the tailor's pillow, he could not get in.

questions.q: How did Simpkin feel when he looked at the hidden silk in the moonlight?
choices: Proud of how clever he was
Ashamed of his badness
Hungry for some more mice
Happy to have kept it
questions.evidence: he felt quite ashamed of his badness compared with those good little mice

questions.q: What was the first thing the tailor saw when he woke on Christmas morning?
choices: The finished coat lying across the end of his bed
A skein of cherry-coloured silk on his quilt
Simpkin asleep on the warm hearth
A little mouse sitting on his pillow
questions.evidence: the first thing which he saw upon the patchwork quilt, was a skein of cherry-coloured twisted silk

questions.q: What was pinned where the last button-hole was missing?
choices: A note that said NO MORE TWIST
A tiny thimble made of silver
A thank-you letter from the Mayor
A little ribbon tied in a bow

questions.q: Who really finished the Mayor's coat?
choices: The tailor, in his sleep
Simpkin the cat
The little mice
The Mayor's own tailor
questions.evidence: they looked as if they had been made by little mice

questions.q: What is this story mostly about?
choices: A cat who learns to sew a fine coat for a Mayor
Mice who help a kind, sick tailor by finishing his coat
A Mayor who gets married on Christmas Day morning
Birds who sing Christmas songs on the roofs of a town
questions.evidence: compared with those good little mice
